requirements.statement: The platform shall allow XATA employees to create, manage, prioritize, track and complete personal and team TODO items.
The solution shall provide a single, centralized web application as the common place to manage TODO items.
Users shall be able to quickly create and update TODO items.
The solution shall provide visibility of open, completed and overdue TODO work.
Team members shall be able to assign TODO items to one another.
The solution shall provide basic priority and due-date management for TODO items.
The solution shall provide a simple dashboard for work tracking.
The first release shall be intentionally small and easy to use.
The solution shall reduce dependency on spreadsheets, email and chat for TODO tracking.
System shall allow an authenticated user to create a TODO.
A TODO shall contain title, description, status, priority and due date. Users shall be able to set priority and due date.
Users shall be able to edit TODOs they own or are authorized to manage.
Users shall be able to mark TODOs as completed.
Users shall be able to assign a TODO to another authorized user.
System shall support Open, In Progress and Completed statuses.
System shall support Low, Medium, High and Critical priorities.
Users shall filter TODOs by status, priority, assignee and due date.
Users shall search TODOs by title or description.
Support user login and a basic user profile.
Users shall be able to view and delete TODOs.
TODOs shall support a description and optional notes.
Provide a dashboard showing TODO status.
Provide a basic team view for assigned TODOs.
Maintain audit information such as created date and updated date for TODOs.
Employee role: create and manage own TODOs, view assigned TODOs, and update status.
Team Lead role: create and assign TODOs, view team TODOs, and monitor overdue work.
Administrator role: manage users and basic platform configuration.
Dashboard shall show Open, In Progress, Completed and Overdue counts. Priority: Must.
Team Leads shall view TODOs assigned to their team members. Priority: Must.
System shall maintain created-by, created-date, updated-by and updated-date for each TODO. Priority: Must.
Users shall be able to delete TODOs where permitted. Priority: Should.
System shall prevent unauthorized modification of another user's TODO. Priority: Must.
System shall provide a web interface through supported browsers. Priority: Must.
Create TODO: enter title; enter description; select priority; select due date; optionally assign to a user; save the TODO.
Manage TODO: view details; edit information; change status; change priority or due date; reassign where authorized; delete where authorized.
Dashboard: show total open TODOs, in-progress TODOs, completed TODOs, overdue TODOs, and high/critical priority TODOs.
A TODO must have a title.
A due date cannot be earlier than creation date unless explicitly permitted.
Completed TODOs must have Completed status.
Only authorized users can assign or modify TODOs.
Overdue means due date has passed and status is not Completed.
Deleting a TODO must not delete the user account or other TODOs.
User can log in and create a TODO.
TODO can be assigned, updated and completed.
Dashboard counts correctly reflect TODO state.
Users cannot modify TODOs outside their authorization.
Filtering and search return correct results.
Application meets agreed NFRs.
XATA can complete the core TODO lifecycle without administrator assistance.
Normal page/API response time must be ≤ 2 seconds for 95% of requests under normal load.
TODO create/update operations must complete in ≤ 2 seconds for 95% of requests.
Dashboard loading must complete in ≤ 3 seconds for 95% of requests.
Search/filter response must be ≤ 2 seconds for 95% of requests.
The platform must support at least 500 concurrent active users.
Monthly availability shall be ≥ 99.5%, excluding agreed maintenance windows.
Planned maintenance shall be communicated at least 24 hours in advance.
Service shall be restored within 30 minutes after an application failure.
The solution shall support growth in users and TODO volume without major redesign.
The solution shall support at least 100,000 TODO records initially.
Application services should be horizontally scalable where practical.
Database design shall support future growth beyond initial capacity.
All users shall be authenticated before accessing protected functionality.
Authorization shall be role-based.
Users shall only access TODO data permitted by their role.
Data shall be encrypted in transit using HTTPS/TLS.
Sensitive credentials shall not be hard-coded.
If passwords are locally managed, they shall use secure industry-standard hashing.
The application shall protect against common web vulnerabilities, including injection, broken access control and XSS.
Administrative actions should be auditable.
TODO records shall have unique identifiers.
Required fields shall be validated server-side.
Updates shall not silently overwrite conflicting data.
Created and updated timestamps shall be stored consistently.
Referential integrity shall be maintained between TODOs and users.
Deleted data handling shall follow XATA's retention policy.
Core create/update/complete flow should require minimal steps.
UI shall be responsive for standard desktop and tablet screens.
Validation errors shall be understandable.
Status, priority and overdue items shall be visually distinguishable.
Common actions shall be discoverable without technical knowledge.
Target WCAG 2.1 AA principles where practical.
Keyboard navigation should support core workflows.
Form controls should have meaningful labels.
Text should have sufficient contrast and readable sizing.
Solution shall use modular, maintainable code.
Business logic shall be separated from presentation and persistence.
APIs and major components shall be documented.
Automated unit tests shall cover critical business logic.
Configuration shall be externalized from source code.
Logging shall support troubleshooting without exposing sensitive information.
Application errors shall be logged with sufficient troubleshooting context.
Health checks shall be available.
Key metrics should include request failures and response latency.
Logs should include correlation/request identifiers where appropriate.
Operational alerts should be configurable for service failures.
Production data shall be backed up according to an agreed schedule.
Backups shall be protected from unauthorized access.
Solution shall support restoration after major failure.
Target RPO: 15 minutes unless XATA agrees otherwise.
Target RTO: 30 minutes.
Support current versions of major enterprise browsers such as Chrome and Edge.
Avoid browser-specific functionality unless approved.
APIs should use documented, versionable interfaces.
Collect only data required for TODO management.
Access to personal/team information shall follow XATA authorization rules.
Sensitive information shall not be written to application logs.
Data retention and deletion shall follow XATA policy.
Critical application/database components shall have documented recovery procedures.
Recovery procedures shall be tested periodically.
XBS shall document dependencies required to restore the service.
XBS shall demonstrate compliance with agreed NFRs through appropriate testing, evidence, configuration review and operational validation before production acceptance.
Security NFR category has priority Must.
Performance NFR category has priority Must.
Availability NFR category has priority Must.
Data Integrity NFR category has priority Must.
Backup & Recovery NFR category has priority Must.
Usability NFR category has priority Must.
Maintainability NFR category has priority Must.
Accessibility NFR category has priority Should.
Advanced observability NFR category has priority Should.

open_questions.question: What does 'quickly' mean for creating and updating TODO items (for example, a target number of steps or time), and how will it be measured?
What is the scope of 'basic' priority and due-date management (for example, priority levels, due-date rules, and overdue definition)?
What is the definition of a 'team' and how are team members grouped for TODO assignment and team-level TODO management?
What content and metrics must the 'simple dashboard' include, and what does 'understand team workload' from the background require beyond the dashboard?
What measurable target defines success for 'reduce dependency on spreadsheets, email and chat', and what is the baseline?

The supplied evidence contains no non-functional requirements (for example security, performance, availability, accessibility, or integration constraints). Are such requirements defined in another source, or are they out of scope for this BRD?
BR-003 refers to TODOs users 'are authorized to manage', but the evidence does not define what authorization applies or which roles hold it.
BR-005 allows assignment to 'another authorized user', but the evidence does not define who is authorized to receive assignments or how authorization is determined.
The in-scope list includes deleting TODOs, but no business requirement or role responsibility states who may delete a TODO or under what conditions.
The evidence does not define 'overdue' for the Team Lead's monitoring responsibility or what 'team' comprises.
The scope of 'basic platform configuration' for the Administrator role is not defined.
The in-scope list includes optional notes, but BR-002 lists only title, description, status, priority and due date. It is unclear whether notes are a required, optional, or separate field.
The level of detail required for the dashboard showing TODO status and the basic team view is not defined.

The supplied evidence contains no non-functional requirements (such as performance, security, availability, or accessibility targets), so it is unclear whether none were specified or they were omitted from the BRD extract.
Which browsers are 'supported browsers' for BR-015, and which versions are in scope?
What rules define 'where permitted' for deletion (BR-013) and 'where authorized' for reassignment and deletion (section 7.2)? Authorization roles and criteria are not specified.

Section 7.3 lists 'Total open TODOs' and 'High/Critical priority TODOs', which are not in BR-010. Is the dashboard required to show these counts, and how is 'Open' (BR-010) distinguished from 'Total open' (7.3)? Also, how is 'Overdue' defined?
How are a Team Lead's team members defined and maintained for the team-view requirement in BR-011?
Who is permitted to approve a due date earlier than the creation date, and under what conditions is this 'explicit permission' given?
How are 'authorized users' defined, and what authorization model governs who can assign, modify, or update TODOs?
What are the 'agreed NFRs'? The NFR evidence is referenced but not included in the supplied evidence, so the non-functional acceptance threshold cannot be determined.
What fields, criteria, and scope are covered by 'filtering and search', and what defines a 'correct' result?
What counts are required on the dashboard, and how is each count defined in terms of TODO state (for example, how overdue TODOs are counted)?

NFR-PERF-001 applies only "under normal load", but the source does not define normal load (for example, the number of concurrent users or request volume). What load profile should the response-time target be measured against?

NFR-PERF-005 requires at least 500 concurrent active users but does not state whether the performance targets in NFR-PERF-001 to NFR-PERF-004 must be met at that concurrency level. Is the 500-user requirement expected to be tested against those response-time targets?

The 95% response-time targets (NFR-PERF-001 to NFR-PERF-004) do not specify the measurement window or sampling method (for example, per day, per hour, or per test run). How should compliance with the 95% threshold be measured?
Which maintenance windows are agreed and excluded from the 99.5% monthly availability target, and how is availability measured?
Who must receive the 24-hour advance communication of planned maintenance, and through which channel?
When does the 30-minute service restoration clock start and stop, and what constitutes restored service?
What time horizon or volume target applies to 'initially' in the 100,000 TODO record requirement, and what defines 'without major redesign'?
Where horizontal scalability is required 'where practical,' what criteria determine when it is not practical?
Is the locally managed password requirement applicable, given that the source does not state whether passwords are locally managed?
Which administrative actions must be auditable, and what is the required audit retention? The 'should' obligation strength is not resolved.
What is XATA's retention policy referenced for deleted data, and where is it defined?
The scope of 'where practical' for WCAG 2.1 AA conformance is undefined. Which success criteria or conformance level must be met, and which exceptions apply?
'Standard desktop and tablet screens' and 'minimal steps' are not quantified. What screen sizes, resolutions, and maximum step counts are expected?
'Critical business logic' for automated unit test coverage is not defined. Which modules or rules are in scope, and is a coverage threshold required?
The set of 'key metrics' beyond request failures and response latency is not specified, and no alert thresholds are given for 'service failures'. Which metrics and thresholds are required?
No BRD evidence was supplied, and the NFR evidence contains no requirement IDs or functional requirements. Are there BRD functional requirements and IDs that must be included in this inventory?
Who agrees the backup schedule, and what is its frequency and retention period? The source says only 'an agreed schedule'.
What constitutes a 'major failure', and what is the restoration time or success criterion after one? The source does not define either.
Who may agree to a different RPO, and what is the process for that agreement? The source says only 'unless XATA agrees otherwise'.
Which browsers and versions are in scope beyond Chrome and Edge? 'Major enterprise browsers' and 'current versions' are not defined.
Who approves browser-specific functionality, and what approval criteria apply?
Which XATA authorization rules and XATA data retention/deletion policies apply? They are referenced but not supplied in the evidence.
How often must recovery procedures be tested? 'Periodically' is not quantified.
What does 'XBS' refer to, and what is the scope of the dependency documentation required to restore the service?

The supplied evidence does not contain the agreed NFR statements, measurable thresholds, units, or time periods for the priority categories; what are the specific agreed NFRs and their acceptance criteria?

The priority table uses Must and Should without defining how Should-priority categories (Accessibility, Advanced observability) differ in acceptance obligation from Must-priority categories; is a Should item required for production acceptance?
